title: Turnip: modeled ₹347/qtl left, Dhanotu (Mandi) → Kangra (Baijnath)
summary: January 2025: reported turnip prices at Dhanotu (Mandi) and Kangra (Baijnath) imply a positive modeled margin after costs on 89% of 18 matched days; a morning-report back-test averages ₹347 per quintal. No actual trade verified.
why_selected: Selected from 62 same-variety market pairs screened for turnip in January 2025; best tested candidate among the bounded set of routed finalists, not a global optimum.

evidence.observations: daily modal prices for the same variety and grade (FAQ) at both markets; sale matched to the first Kangra (Baijnath) report 1–3 days after purchase
caveats: Back-test on reported prices: no actual shipment, buyer or seller is claimed.
Modal prices are reported daily aggregates, not offers anyone could be sure to get.
This data has no arrival volumes, so it cannot show whether the destination could absorb more supply; no capital-constrained or volume allocation optimum is claimed.

Costs extrapolate onion survey values (including to other crops) plus stated allowances, not freight quotes; OSRM car routing, not a verified truck route. Representative town points may not be at mandi gates.
Historical: this says what paid then, not what pays today.

scenes.headline: January 2025
scenes.caption: Dhanotu (Mandi) (Himachal Pradesh) and Kangra (Baijnath) (Himachal Pradesh) both reported turnip prices for the same variety and grade (FAQ) on 18 matched days.

scenes.headline: Two markets, two prices
scenes.caption: Dhanotu (Mandi) reported a median ₹1,250 per quintal. Kangra (Baijnath) reported a median ₹1,650 around modeled arrival days. These are not offers.

scenes.headline: Gap ₹400/qtl
scenes.caption: The median gap was ₹400 per quintal, and Kangra (Baijnath) was dearer on 94% of days.

scenes.headline: 150 km by road
scenes.caption: 150 km on OpenStreetMap roads (~3 hours by car). A loaded truck is slower, so we allow 1 days plus 7 days to get paid.

scenes.headline: After modeled costs
scenes.caption: Freight ≈₹32/qtl, 5% fees and commission, loading, 5% loss and interest. On the typical day ₹210 per quintal was left.

scenes.headline: Still positive under stress
scenes.caption: With 25% dearer freight, 10% loss and costlier credit, the typical day still kept ₹119 per quintal.

scenes.headline: A trader who only knew the morning's news
scenes.caption: Using only the latest available Kangra (Baijnath) report, the rule selects 16 of 18 modeled shipping days. 16 had positive modeled net, averaging ₹347 per quintal (₹256 under stress).

scenes.headline: The back-test
scenes.caption: The modeled Turnip route from Dhanotu (Mandi) to Kangra (Baijnath) was positive on 89% of matched days in January 2025. At that average, a 100-quintal (10-tonne) load implies ₹34,700, or ₹25,600 under stress. Actual buyer, capacity, haggling, rejection and delays are unknown.

assumptions.value: onion survey freight applied per quintal to turnip
scaled by road km against the 1,115 km Lasalgaon→Azadpur route → ₹32/qtl here
12% a year (14% adverse) for transit + 7 days
~450 road km a day → 1 days here

conclusion: The modeled Turnip route from Dhanotu (Mandi) to Kangra (Baijnath) was positive on 89% of matched days in January 2025. At that average, a 100-quintal (10-tonne) load implies ₹34,700, or ₹25,600 under stress. Actual buyer, capacity, haggling, rejection and delays are unknown.

sources.title: Agmarknet / data.gov.in daily mandi modal prices (retained AGRINET snapshot)
RBI Working Paper WPS (DEPR) 08/2024 — Price Dynamics of Tomato, Onion and Potato
